I am 76 years old, and my back is not what it used to be. I only started farming last year after I came back to the village—I spent my life doing other work, and now my son helped me get this 5.5 mu of land. I never went to school, so I cannot read the words on the fertilizer bags. I go to the seed shop in town, ask the shopkeeper what my neighbors are buying, and I watch the other farmers in Quzhou closely. My wife and I are just two people, so we cannot handle too much land or too many different things.

This is how I will manage my land. I will put 4 mu into the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what every household here does—the winter wheat goes in after the autumn harvest, and then the summer maize goes in immediately after we cut the wheat in June. The other 1.5 mu I will plant with cotton, because my wife knows how to pick cotton and we need some cash income, but 1.5 mu is all my old arms can manage for such a labor-heavy crop. I have a well, so when the sky does not give rain, I will pump water. I do not have the strength for deep ploughing anymore, so I will use the rotary tiller for the wheat and the cotton. For the summer maize, everyone plants it directly into the wheat stubble without turning the soil, so I will do no-tillage for the maize just like them.

For seeds, I will buy the improved wheat variety and the hybrid maize that the agricultural shop recommends—they say these are the kinds tested by the university people in Quzhou, and my neighbors use them too. For cotton, I will use the improved seeds as well. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer when I sow, and then topdress with urea when the crops are growing tall and look hungry. I will irrigate the wheat three times, the maize twice, and the cotton three times. I will spray pesticides when I see worms or aphids, or when my neighbors start spraying—three times for wheat, twice for maize, and four times for cotton because cotton attracts more pests. I expect my wheat to give about 460 kg per mu, the maize about 500 kg per mu, and the cotton about 95 kg per mu. These are not high numbers, but I am old and still learning, and I know my limits.
